Chapter 3: The Man Who Felled the Golden Spruce—Obsession, Crisis, and the Breaking Point.
Every community has folks who just don’t quite fit in. Sometimes, it’s just this quiet, nagging feeling—like something important’s slipped away and nobody really notices. Other times, it’s an energy that builds and builds, until you feel like you just have to do something, even if you’re not sure how it’ll all turn out.
On Haida Gwaii, there was one man like that. Someone shaped by the forests themselves—and by all the forces that threatened them.
Now, he wasn’t your classic villain. In fact, like so many drawn to the islands, he was just looking for meaning. Trying to make sense of a world that felt more chaotic and unfair with every passing year. He’d spent time working in the logging industry, seen with his own eyes the destruction from clear-cutting, and felt this heavy responsibility for everything that was being lost.
That frustration slowly burned into anger. And after a while, the anger turned into something even stronger—a full-blown obsession.
For years, he watched as the forests vanished, the land carved up by roads and machines. He tried to warn people, to open their eyes to what was happening—but most folks just kept their heads down, busy with their own lives. The more he spoke out and was ignored, the lonelier he felt. That isolation only fed his desperation.
So, imagine being in that state of mind. He started to see the golden spruce as more than just a tree. To him, it became a symbol—a living, breathing reminder of how people were fooling themselves. As long as the tree stood, he thought, everyone could pretend things weren’t so bad. But if it was gone? Maybe, just maybe, people would finally wake up and see what was really at stake.
Making the decision wasn’t easy. Doubt crept in, and guilt too—moments where he wondered if he was doing the right thing. But the urgency kept building, until it drowned out everything else. In the end, he went by himself, slipping quietly through the darkness toward that tree, which had become both a guiding light and a target.
The act itself? It was shockingly quick. Just a few cuts, a final push—and the golden spruce fell. Its branches crashed to the forest floor. In that instant, he felt a strange mix of relief and sorrow, as if he’d finally let go of a weight but lost something precious at the same time.
Word spread fast. The community reeled. For the Haida people, losing the golden spruce wasn’t just about a tree—it cut to the heart of who they were. For others, it was a jolt, a wake-up call. A reminder that one person’s actions can ripple out, touching lives and stories in ways nobody can predict.
Afterward, the man vanished. He left behind confusion, questions, and a community trying to make sense of what had happened. Some saw him as unhinged, others as a kind of martyr. Most people were just stunned—caught between grief and disbelief. The golden spruce was gone, but its legacy—and the questions it raised—were just beginning.
